Abstract Post‐exertional malaise and delayed recovery are hallmark symptoms of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome ( ME / CFS ). Studies on repeated cardiopulmonary exercise testing ( CPET ) show that previous exercise negatively affects oxygen uptake ( VO 2 ) and power output ( PO ) in ME / CFS . Whether this affects arterial lactate concentrations ([La a ]) is unknown. We studied 18 female patients (18–50 years) fulfilling the Canadian Consensus Criteria for ME / CFS and 15 healthy females (18–50 years) who underwent repeated CPET s 24 h apart ( CPET 1 and CPET 2 ) with [La a ] measured every 30th second. VO 2 at peak exercise ( VO 2peak ) was lower in patients than in controls on CPET 1 ( P < 0.001) and decreased in patients on CPET 2 ( P < 0.001). However, the difference in VO 2peak between CPET s did not differ significantly between groups. [La a ] per PO was higher in patients during both CPET s ( P interaction < 0.001), but increased in patients and decreased in controls from CPET 1 to CPET 2 ( P interaction < 0.001). Patients had lower VO 2 ( P = 0.02) and PO ( P = 0.002) at the gas exchange threshold ( GET , the point where CO 2 production increases relative to VO 2 ), but relative intensity (% VO 2peak ) and [La a ] at GET did not differ significantly from controls on CPET 1 . Patients had a reduction in VO 2 ( P = 0.02) and PO ( P = 0.01) at GET on CPET 2 , but no significant differences in % VO 2peak and [La a ] at GET between CPET s. Controls had no significant differences in VO 2 , PO or % VO 2peak at GET between CPET s, but [La a ] at GET was reduced on CPET 2 ( P = 0.008). In conclusion, previous exercise deteriorates physical performance and increases [La a ] during exercise in patients with ME / CFS while it lowers [La a ] in healthy subjects. Introduction Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) is a complex, multisystem and often debilitating disorder of unknown etiology (Institute of Medicine 2015 ). Common symptoms include fatigue, post‐exertional malaise (PEM), widespread pain, sleep disturbances, cognitive dysfunction, sensory hypersensitivity, orthostatic intolerance, and gastrointestinal discomfort. There are no reliable diagnostic markers or clinical findings that can verify the diagnosis, which is based on self‐reported symptoms. There is no widely accepted agreement regarding diagnostic criteria. The Canadian Consensus Criteria (CCC) (Carruthers et al. 2003 ) and The International Consensus Criteria (ICC) (Carruthers et al. 2011 ) both appear to identify a subgroup of patients with more severe functional impairments, as well as marked physical and cognitive symptoms (Jason et al. 2013 ). PEM is defined as a substantial worsening of symptoms after mild to moderate physical, mental, or emotional exertion. PEM and impaired recovery after exertion are mandatory criteria in both the CCC and the ICC. Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) provides an accurate and objective assessment of functional capacity (ATS/ACCP Statement on cardiopulmonary exercise testing, 2003 ; Arena et al. 2007 ). Repeated CPET have demonstrated that ME/CFS patients are unable to reproduce oxygen uptake and power output at peak exercise (VO 2peak ) and/or at the gas exchange threshold defined by the V‐slope method, when tested on two consecutive days (Vermeulen et al. 2010 ; Snell et al. 2013 ; Keller et al. 2014 ; Nelson et al. 2019 ). The gas exchange threshold is the point where VCO 2 increases relative to VO 2, and has traditionally been viewed as a transition from aerobic to anaerobic energy production, coinciding with the onset of lactate accumulation. However, the notion of tissue hypoxia as the main cause of lactate accumulation is no longer accepted (Brooks 2018 ). Lactate is always the end result of glycolysis, also under aerobic conditions (Rogatzki et al. 2015 ). Glycolysis increases during exercise, and lactate is rapidly cleared from the circulation, mainly through oxidation and gluconeogenesis. During an incremental exercise test, blood lactate accumulation occurs when the rate of lactate appearance exceeds the rate of lactate disposal (Brooks 2018 ). Trained individuals have a lower blood lactate concentration and increased lactate metabolic clearance rate for an absolute exercise intensity, compared to untrained individuals. However, the rate of lactate appearance has been found to be similar in trained and untrained subjects at the same relative intensity defined as percent of VO 2peak (%VO 2peak ) (Bergman et al. 1999 ; Messonnier et al. 2013 ). Previous studies have not demonstrated consistent results with regard to physical performance and lactate accumulation in ME/CFS (Riley et al. 1990 ; Wong et al. 1992 ; Gibson et al. 1993 ; Lane et al. 1998 ; Sargent et al. 2002 ; Jammes et al. 2005 ), but lactate accumulation during repeated exercise testing has not been examined. The aim of this study was therefore to examine if VO 2 and arterial plasma lactate concentrations at various exercise intensities differed between patients with ME/CFS and healthy controls by performing two CPETs 24 h apart.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the physiological and biochemical responses, including oxygen uptake, power output, and arterial lactate concentrations, during two maximal incremental cycle ergometer tests performed 24 hours apart in female Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) patients compared to healthy controls. The findings revealed that previous exercise deteriorates physical performance and increases lactate accumulation in ME/CFS patients, while it improves lactate handling in healthy subjects, indicating a disturbed metabolic response to exertion in ME/CFS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Repeated Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing (CPET), specifically maximal incremental ramp tests.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two maximal incremental ramp tests (CPET 1 and CPET 2) were performed 24 hours apart on a cycle ergometer. Each test included a 2-min resting phase and 2 min of unloaded pedaling, followed by a linear increase in power output until volitional exhaustion. Increment rates were individually set (10-24 W/min for ME/CFS patients; 15-30 W/min for controls) to reach VO2peak within 8-12 min. Arterial lactate concentrations were measured every 30 seconds during exercise. Blood sampling during CPET 1 amounted to approximately 150–200 mL. No specific dose-response comparisons for different fixed exercise intensities were reported beyond the comparisons between the two repeated tests.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Whole-body physiological measurement derived from respiratory gas exchange
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Oxygen Uptake (Physiological measure of consumption rate)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower in patients than in controls on CPET 1 (P < 0.001); decreased significantly in patients on CPET 2 (P < 0.001) but not in controls. The difference in VO2peak between CPETs did not differ significantly between groups. Absolute change in patients was considered too small to indicate a major change in exercise tolerance, though an expected mean reduction of 0.68 mL/kg/min was calculated based on hemoglobin reduction.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Maximal capacity of the body to transport and utilize oxygen during incremental exercise, reflecting aerobic fitness.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Peak exercise during repeated cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) in female ME/CFS patients compared to healthy controls.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates impaired physical performance and functional capacity, suggesting reduced exercise tolerance in ME/CFS patients, especially after previous exertion, though the absolute magnitude was considered too small to fully explain post-exertional malaise by the authors.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Resting [La a ] did not differ between patients and controls before CPET 1 but was significantly different before CPET 2 between groups. Generally higher in ME/CFS patients than controls during both CPETs, particularly when normalized per power output and PO kg (P interaction < 0.001), with the difference increasing from CPET 1 to CPET 2 (P interaction < 0.001). Patients showed a leftward shift of the lactate curve from CPET 1 to CPET 2 (P < 0.001), while controls showed a rightward shift (P < 0.001). [La a ] at GET did not differ significantly from controls on CPET 1 in patients, and showed no significant differences between CPETs in patients, but was significantly reduced in controls on CPET 2 (P = 0.008). The difference in [La a ] at GET from CPET 1 to CPET 2 was significantly different between groups. [La a ] at Lactate Turnpoint (LT) was not significantly different between groups on CPET 1, but was significantly reduced in controls from CPET 1 to CPET 2, with the difference between CPETs significantly different between groups. Detection limit: 0.044 mmol/L; linearity limit: 16.85 mmol/L.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicator of anaerobic metabolism and metabolic stress during exercise, reflecting the balance between lactate production and clearance, the efficiency of oxidative phosphorylation, and overall energy metabolism.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Resting and during repeated maximal incremental cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET 1 and CPET 2 performed 24 hours apart) in female ME/CFS patients and healthy controls, analyzed per power output and at gas exchange threshold (GET) and lactate turnpoint (LT).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher [La a ] per power output, a left-shifted lactate curve, and increased lactate accumulation over repeated tests indicate impaired exercise tolerance, increased reliance on anaerobic metabolism, disturbed energy metabolism, and/or reduced oxidative capacity, particularly in ME/CFS patients, contributing to post-exertional malaise (PEM). Reduced [La a ] at GET or LT in controls suggests better metabolic adaptation and improved lactate disposal/clearance ability following prior exercise.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: VO2 at GET (Oxygen uptake at Gas Exchange Threshold)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Whole-body physiological measurement derived from respiratory gas exchange
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Oxygen Uptake (Physiological measure of consumption rate)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower in patients than controls on CPET 1 (P = 0.02). Decreased significantly in patients on CPET 2 (P = 0.02) but not in controls. Occurred at a significantly lower VO2 in patients compared to controls.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Marks the transition to increased reliance on anaerobic metabolism during exercise; an indicator of aerobic fitness and endurance capacity.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Gas exchange threshold (GET) during repeated cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) in female ME/CFS patients compared to healthy controls.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower VO2 at GET indicates reduced aerobic capacity, earlier reliance on anaerobic metabolism, and functional limitation at this threshold in ME/CFS patients.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Power output at GET (Gas Exchange Threshold)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Whole-body physiological measurement (derived from exercise intensity)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Power Output (Physiological measure of exercise intensity)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower in patients than controls on CPET 1 (P = 0.002). Significant reduction in patients on CPET 2 (P = 0.01) but no significant reduction in controls on CPET 2. Occurred at a significantly lower absolute power output in patients.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Represents the work capacity or exercise intensity at the gas exchange threshold, where ventilation increases disproportionately to oxygen uptake.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Gas exchange threshold (GET) during repeated cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) in female ME/CFS patients compared to healthy controls.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower values indicate reduced work capacity and impaired physical performance and endurance capacity at the gas exchange threshold in ME/CFS patients. Inability to reproduce power output at GET in ME/CFS patients is a consistent finding, suggesting impaired exercise tolerance and post-exertional malaise.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not differ significantly from controls on CPET 1; no significant differences between CPETs in patients; no significant differences in controls between CPETs.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Represents the relative effort or intensity achieved at the gas exchange threshold.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Gas exchange threshold (GET) during repeated cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) in female ME/CFS patients compared to healthy controls.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests that the relative intensity at GET may be similar despite absolute reductions in VO2 and PO in ME/CFS patients.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Similar between groups at CPET 1 and CPET 2 initially. However, it decreased by 0.7 g/dL in both study groups from CPET 1 to CPET 2, a reduction that could explain an expected mean reduction in peak VO2 of 0.68 mL/kg/min.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Primary protein responsible for oxygen transport from the lungs to the body's tissues.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: At rest before CPET 1 and within 90 seconds after peak exercise on CPET 1 and CPET 2, and between CPETs, in female ME/CFS patients and healthy controls.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Consistent levels initially suggest no differential acute changes in oxygen carrying capacity due to exercise or underlying health conditions. The observed reduction between CPETs indicates a decreased oxygen-carrying capacity, which contributes to reduced peak oxygen uptake and overall exercise capacity in both groups, but is relevant for understanding performance changes.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Power output at OBLA (Onset of Blood Lactate Accumulation)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Not directly measured in tissue/fluid; a physiological measure derived from exercise intensity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly in controls from CPET 1 to CPET 2. Decreased significantly in patients from CPET 1 to CPET 2. The difference in power output at OBLA from CPET 1 to CPET 2 was significantly different between groups.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Represents the exercise intensity at which blood lactate concentration reaches 4 mmol/L, indicating a significant reliance on anaerobic metabolism.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Repeated Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing (CPET 1 and CPET 2 after 24 hours) in ME/CFS patients vs. healthy controls.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects endurance capacity. Decreased in ME/CFS patients suggests impaired exercise tolerance and worsened metabolic response to repeated exertion. Increased in controls suggests improved lactate clearance/aerobic capacity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Upregulated expression in PBMCs from ME/CFS patients.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Inhibits pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, thereby regulating pyruvate flux into the Krebs cycle and favoring glucose for anaerobic metabolism.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Proposes a disturbed PDK regulation in ME/CFS patients, potentially limiting pyruvate flux and affecting lactate clearance through oxidation, contributing to disturbed energy metabolism.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated levels in blood compared to healthy controls.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A major component of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria, indicating bacterial translocation/inflammation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: In ME/CFS patients compared to healthy controls, especially with exercise leading to increased bacterial translocation.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests increased bacterial translocation in ME/CFS patients, possibly contributing to post-exertional malaise (PEM) and affecting metabolism through inflammation and/or elevated catecholamines.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in myoblasts grown in presence of serum from severe ME/CFS patients.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cellular energy production, part of aerobic metabolism.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Myoblasts grown in presence of serum from severe ME/CFS patients.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates disturbed energy metabolism in ME/CFS patients.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in myoblasts grown in presence of serum from severe ME/CFS patients.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Release of lactate from cells, a byproduct of glycolysis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Myoblasts grown in presence of serum from severe ME/CFS patients.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates disturbed energy metabolism and potentially increased anaerobic glycolysis in ME/CFS patients.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Impaired maximal respiration capacity compared to healthy PBMCs.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cellular energy production, ability to respond to metabolic stress.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: PBMCs from ME/CFS patients compared to healthy PBMCs.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests an inability to adequately increase respiratory rate in response to elevated metabolic stress in ME/CFS patients, indicating disturbed energy metabolism.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Impaired AMPK phosphorylation in cells from ME/CFS patients compared to healthy muscle cells.

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates disturbed energy metabolism and impaired cellular response to exercise-like stress in ME/CFS patients.
